{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -c 1
#   -p priority
#   -t 2-00:00
#   --mem 4G
#   -o logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake_%A.log
#   -e logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake_%A.log

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  -c 1 \
  --time=48h \
  --queue=priority \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p logs/rc-nonallelespec

# NOTE: Slurm --mem 4G has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm output naming uses %A (job id). Flux has no portable equivalent.
# Best-effort: use Flux job id and preserve combined stdout/stderr to the same file.
exec >"logs/rc-nonallelespec/snakemake_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.log" 2>&1

module unload python
module load gcc conda2 slurm-drmaa/1.1.1
conda activate rctest

# NOTE: This workflow uses Snakemake --drmaa with Slurm-specific sbatch/srun options inside the DRMAA string.
# There is no universally portable way to translate this "cluster submission" layer to Flux within this script.
# Performance implication: per-rule resource requests and scheduling will not be handled by Flux as intended;
# running many tasks may oversubscribe this single allocation, slow down substantially, or fail.
# You may need a Flux-native Snakemake executor/profile or to run with local execution within the allocation.

snakemake \
  --snakefile src/20_62_nonallelespec_rc-test-Snakefile.py \
  --jobs 9980 \
  --restart-times 0 \
  --cluster-config config/rc-test-snakemake-cluster.json \
  --latency-wait 120 \
  --drmaa " -c {cluster.cores} -p {cluster.partition} --mem={cluster.mem} -t {cluster.time} -o {cluster.out} -e {cluster.err} -J {cluster.J}"

conda deactivate
'
"
}
